name: RSWM Ltd
title: RSWM Ltd - 500350 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: RSWM FY26 PAT turned positive at ₹52 crore (1.1% margin) from a ₹41 crore loss, while revenue fell 5.6% to ₹4,554 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was ₹1,142 crore, up 4.5% QoQ but down 9.1% YoY, with exports at ₹368 crore (up 11.4% QoQ) and domestic sales at ₹774 crore. Q4 EBITDA was ₹85 crore at a 7.4% margin, up 115 bps YoY. For FY26, EBITDA rose 40.5% to ₹327 crore (7.1% margin, up 231 bps), helped by a ₹22.66 crore deferred tax liability write-back under the new tax regime. Management attributed the turnaround mainly to product-mix optimisation, exit from Chhata spinning (~₹250 crore revenue), working capital control and lower finance cost, and said it is not cyclical. Denim and knit were hit by gas disruption in March and by weak US/EU export demand, with utilisation expected to recover by 7-10 points.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of ₹41 crore (-0.9%) in FY25
from ₹29 crore, +74.5%, mainly gain on sale of non-core assets

segments.name: Denim
segments.commentary: Utilisation above 80%, targeted at 85-90%; March production lost for some days due to gas disruption. Gas availability is back in April, but gas prices have risen sharply. Yarn costs (cotton and polyester-cotton) also pushed denim input costs up.

segments.name: Knit
segments.commentary: Utilisation was below 80%, with a target of above 85%. Capacity is being expanded from about 600 tons to 900 tons, including 120 tons of printing, at a ₹92 crore capex. Management expects 3-4% EBITDA improvement once the full product range is in place in Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Mélange yarn
segments.commentary: Utilisation was 65-70%, expected to return to 85-90% within this or the next quarter, as most sales are export-linked through garmenters.

segments.name: Synthetic and fibre (incl. recycled PET)
segments.commentary: Described as utilised optimally and more domestic, with lower disruption. The 130 metric tons per day polyester fibre business uses 60 lakh recycled bottles daily.

segments.name: Cotton spinning (Chhata)
segments.commentary: Operations were curtailed for inefficiency, removing about ₹250 crore of annual revenue. Management says the spindle-closure journey is largely done, with no further closures planned for the current and next quarter.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 expected to be slightly better or equal to Q4 FY26, per management's outlook on the current quarter.
Utilisation in denim, knit and mélange expected to improve by 7-10% from Q4 levels in coming quarters.
Double-digit EBITDA margin is the aspiration, dependent on demand normalisation and internal execution; no timeline given beyond 'as early as possible'.
US order book described as under recovery; management expects about two more quarters to normalise.
Management said RSWM can reach ₹6,200-6,500 crore revenue in three to four years, calling it possible.
Power cost savings of about ₹1 per unit from Adani renewable tie-up, roughly 3-4 lakh units per day (about ₹1 crore per month).
capex_capacity: B2B (recycled PET) project at Ratlam, Madhya Pradesh: total capex ₹427 crore, funded about 70% by project loan (₹300 crore sanctioned) and the balance by equity and holding-company loans. Construction to start mid-May 2026, with operations targeted for Q1 FY28.
Knit expansion of ₹92 crore: capacity from about 600 tons to 900 tons, including printing; full rollout targeted in Q3 FY27.
No other major capex planned beyond the knit expansion and plant modernisation; capex to focus on projects with 1-3 year payback.
Renewable energy: about 70% of energy mix now from wind and solar under the Adani round-the-clock tie-up.
Preferential issue of 24.7 lakh convertible warrants (about ₹36 crore) to LNJ Textile Advisory LLP, a promoter group entity, approved by the Board in April 2026.
demand_pricing: Global textile demand described as soft, with discretionary spending in Western markets cautious; the US tariff situation and the Gulf conflict disrupted trade flows and freight.
Price pass-through lags cost increases, especially in denim, where yarn, gas, dyes and freight have all risen; orders already booked cannot be repriced.
Yarn businesses are said to maintain spreads, with improvement in B2B yarn spreads.
Revenue decline came from the Chhata spinning exit (~₹250 crore) and weaker US-linked exports after the tariffs in Q3.
Management expects UK, EU and New Zealand FTAs to become operational around the end of 2026 or early 2027. The value-added share of sales is under one-fifth, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the recovery comes from product mix, discounts, energy, inventory discipline or exits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the turnaround is internally driven, mainly product-mix optimisation and cutting low-contribution volumes, plus working-capital tightening (about ₹12.5 crore of interest savings). It did not give a percentage split.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US order book fully recovered after the tariff settlement?
qa_highlights.answer: Not fully. Management said it is under recovery; product development lost over three to six months is still affecting orders, and it expects about two more quarters to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Adani renewable power tie-up cut power costs, and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated savings of about ₹1 per unit, around 3-4 lakh units per day (roughly ₹1 crore per month), varying by season with wind and solar output.

qa_highlights.question: What PAT impact came from the deferred tax reversal?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹23 crore. Management said PAT would have been ₹29 crore under the existing tax rates.

qa_highlights.question: What is the B2B project funding structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Total cost ₹427 crore, about 70% project financing (₹300 crore loan approved), with the remainder from equity and holding-company loans (about ₹127 crore). The project was scaled down by 60-65% from the original ₹700-plus crore plan.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said term loans are about ₹700 crore and working capital borrowings about ₹800 crore. Term loans are expected to reduce over the next three to four years.

risks_watch: Gas cost inflation from Gulf disruption and possible further supply interruptions for denim and knit.
Pass-through lag on yarn and dye/chemical cost increases, which may keep denim and knit spreads under pressure.
Whether US and EU demand recovers; US order book is still under recovery.
Execution of the ₹427 crore Ratlam recycled PET project, with debt-heavy funding (about 70% loan) and a Q1 FY28 commissioning target.
Sustainability of the FY26 turnaround: Q4 PAT was ₹52 crore for the full year, with the deferred tax write-back contributing a one-off.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the turnaround and margins, but cautious on near-term demand. Management was candid about the Gulf-related gas, freight and pass-through headwinds, and was less specific on quantified targets such as double-digit EBITDA and the 15% CAGR question.
key_quotes: Our focus has been on improving the quality of earnings rather than chasing only volumes at a cost, and the approach is now beginning to reflect in our margins and overall profitability.
And this is not a cyclical thing. The year under consideration has been really very tough for us as well as for the entire textile industry.
So, the turnaround which we are seeing is more because of internal operations than market-led.

adds.what: Knit expansion: capacity from about 600 tons to 900 tons, incl. 120 tons printing (₹92 crore capex)
B2B recycled PET plant at Ratlam, Madhya Pradesh (total capex ₹427 crore)

growth.why: Management guides Q1 FY27 EBITDA flat to slightly better, utilisation up 7-10 points across denim, knit and mélange, and a knit expansion (600 to 900 tons, ₹92 crore) fully rolled out in Q3 FY27, but no explicit revenue growth guidance; the ₹6,200-6,500 crore three-to-four-year revenue ambition is aspirational and FY26 revenue fell 5.6%.
